page.overview:
What is Irem?

Irem, or Irim, is a legendary city mentioned multiple times in the Cthulhu Mythos stories of H. P. Lovecraft, Robert Bloch, and August Derleth.

It was the City of Pillars visited by the Mad Arab in the deserts of Arabia.

Irem is first mentioned by Lovecraft in "The Nameless City", in which the narrator finds evidence of a sapient reptile species that flourished before mankind and built a city in the Arabian desert. One of the images in their murals depicts a human being torn to pieces by the reptiles. The narrator muses that the man in the picture might have been "a pioneer of ancient Irem, the City of Pillars", thus implying that the reptile inhabitants of the Nameless City might have been enemies of the human inhabitants of Irem.

Abdul Alhazred, the 8th century author of the Necronomicon who worshiped Yog-Sothoth and Cthulhu, claimed to have seen Irem, the City of Pillars, "and to have found beneath the ruins of a certain nameless desert town the shocking annals and secrets of a race older than mankind". (: "History of the Necronomicon")
